domain_label: Ludhiana Yarn & Fibre Sourcing and Supply for a Warm-Climate D2C Knitwear Line
purpose: A session-bounded method for the owner of a small AI-designed D2C knitwear brand to source the yarn for a climate-first 3-article California line (A1 cotton-blend 12GG 12-month core, A2 fine-acrylic value driver, A3 merino/lambswool seasonal premium capsule), by recognizing that yarn price is NOT the binding constraint (~$1-2.50 of fibre per garment [ESTIMATE]) and that the two things that actually bind the line are the dye-lot MOQ per colour (~150-500 kg/colour => only ~2-4 launch colours [ESTIMATE]) and the yarn-in-to-ex-factory lead time (~6-12 weeks [ESTIMATE], avoid the Jul-Oct cluster peak); then choosing the source split (buy acrylic/blend/cotton/lambswool in-cluster on bought-dyed stock shades from Vardhman/Sportking/Nahar/Oswal, import only merino tops and cashmere), gating quality as a contractual anti-pill spec (ICI Pilling Box grade >=3-4 post-wash, 25% USTER on mainstream lots), making the dye call (launch on bought-dyed stock shades, NEVER own a dyehouse, graduate to greige + job-work dye only for a proven hero colour), and hardening the system against stale price anchors and supplier failure.
assumptions: no live mandi/importer quote dataset is supplied; price, MOQ, and lead-time bands are reasoned [ESTIMATE] bands keyed to the yarn deep-dive, not invoices, and every underlying point-anchor is treated as stale

the brand runs the deep-dive's climate-first 3-article line: A1 cotton-blend 12GG core, A2 fine-acrylic value driver (7-12GG), A3 merino/lambswool seasonal capsule (Nov-Feb), selling in warm Turlock/Central-Valley California
the geography is the Ludhiana knitwear cluster (~14,000 MSMEs) for spun yarn plus AU/NZ-origin merino tops and imported cashmere held by warehousing importers, in the mid-2020s

supplier-to-named-firm links are representative inference, not confirmed contracts; only the integrated-spinner roster (Vardhman, Sportking, Nahar, Oswal) and the import origins (AU/NZ merino, imported cashmere) are structurally documented in the deep-dive

every money/MOQ/lead-time figure is a labelled [ESTIMATE] band with stated confidence and a live-quote confirmation path; no named-firm price is asserted as [FACT], and premium-fibre price rows are order-of-magnitude only

the brand is a micro-buyer with no in-house metrology (a USTER tester is six-figure-USD class), so quality is enforced as a contractual PO clause plus third-party/spinner-lab testing, not owned instruments
exclusions: any named-firm yarn price, MOQ, or margin stated as [FACT] (only labelled [ESTIMATE] bands and true-by-definition count identities are asserted as anchors)
knitting-machine selection, gauge programming, and linker capacity (covered by the machines specialist, T3)
garment manufacturing economics, CMT costing, and the make-vs-buy boundary beyond naming the yarn/greige buy decision (covered by the manufacturing-economics specialist, T4)

ocean freight India->US, US landed-cost math, the US finished-garment duty computation (heading 6110), and unit economics are covered by the logistics specialist (T9; only the ex-factory lead-time and the by-fibre US duty direction are named here); the India-side raw-fibre import duty on imported merino/superfine tops and cashmere (entering India for the Ludhiana spin) is a DISTINCT layer, NOT the US 6110 garment duty and never collapsed into it -- held [UNKNOWN], mapped to DECISION_MEMO G5 (forward India duty), computation still deferred to T9, no India duty rate invented
the thread-checker device design, full QC metrology, and AQL inspection mechanics beyond naming the contractual gate (covered by the quality specialist, T5)
post-knit finishing chemistry (mercerise, singe, bio-polish, heat-set) beyond naming it as the last pilling lever (covered by the finishing specialist, T6); brand positioning and CAC (covered by T7)

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DYE_METHOD_DECISION states launch-on-bought-dyed-stock-shades as default, NEVER own a dyehouse (NGT/CETP closure risk), and graduate to greige + job-work dye only for a proven hero colour, with the lot-to-lot shade-match (delta-E/fastness) mitigation

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DYEHOUSE_REGULATORY_GATE cites the CPCB/NGT CETP-noncompliance enforcement that makes dyeing the highest-regulatory-risk node, and LEAD_TIME_CALENDAR states the ~6-12 wk yarn-in->ex-factory band and the Jul-Oct peak to avoid

competency_questions.question: How is yarn cost modelled honestly without fabricating a named-firm price, and how is an estimate band labelled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COST_BENCHMARK_HONESTY derives fibre cost as a labelled [ESTIMATE] band (price band x grams/garment) tagged with confidence and a live-quote confirmation path, refuses stale point-anchors, and holds premium rows as order-of-magnitude only

competency_questions.question: How does the brand harden the sourcing system against stale-price shocks, single-supplier failure, and the Jul-Oct contention, and on what cadence is it reviewed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RESILIENCE_BACKUP names a backup spinner/importer and a substitution rule per critical fibre; SOURCING_REVIEW_LOOP sets a price/availability review cadence and the triggers (price spike, supplier loss, peak season, regulatory action) that re-run the plan

glossary.definition: An integrated Ludhiana spinning mill; the roster (Vardhman, Sportking, Nahar, Oswal) is [FACT] (structurally documented in the deep-dive), carrying acrylic/blend/cotton/lambswool count availability, shade cards and restock. Large integrated spinners AS A CLASS typically run in-house USTER-class lab QC [ESTIMATE: industry-lore, MED-HIGH]; whether any SPECIFIC named firm operates such a lab today and will certify our small clause-bound lot is [UNKNOWN] until a live quote/audit (else budget a third-party spot-check). The default source for the A1 cotton-core and A2 acrylic-value articles on bought-dyed stock shades.

The minimum dyed quantity a dye-house will run for one shade (floor ~150-500 kg/colour [ESTIMATE]; economic ~500-2,000 kg; +20-50% small-batch surcharge below); at ~300-400 g/sweater this caps a micro-capsule at ~2-4 launch colours, making it THE binding commercial constraint that sizes the brand, not yarn price.

Yarn purchased already dyed to a spinner's shade-card colour, so the dye-lot and the NGT/closure risk sit on the supplier; the launch default that trades colour control and lot-to-lot shade-match risk for speed and zero dyehouse exposure.

Buying greige (undyed) yarn and paying a dyer a per-kg conversion charge to dye it; wins only once a specific colour is a proven hero worth the dye-lot MOQ and the extra lead time and shade-consistency management, never as the launch default.

The contractual quality gate that defends against pilling, the #1 return driver: an anti-pill / higher-dpf acrylic grade plus an ICI Pilling Box (ISO 12945-1) grade >=3-4 after >=1 home-wash, written as numbers in the PO rather than the adjective 'anti-pill'.

A PO clause requiring the yarn lot to grade at or better than the 25th USTER percentile on CV% and IPI (better than 75% of world production) with thin/thick/nep sensitivities, hairiness band, min tenacity, and count-CV ceiling; the mainstream bar for mass acrylic/cotton -- demanding 5% USTER on a mass lot is unquotable or luxury-priced.

The genuine in-cluster edge a Ludhiana-based buyer gets on the everyday fibres: cost, MOQ flex, shade cards, restock, and -- as a class-level convention of large integrated spinners [ESTIMATE], any specific firm's certification [UNKNOWN] until audited -- in-house lab QC on acrylic/blend/cotton/lambswool that imported supply cannot match -- strongest for A1 cotton-core and A2 acrylic-value, and the reason only merino tops and cashmere are imported.

The fibre cost/quality ladder both analysts arrived at: acrylic (cost floor, Ludhiana's native fibre, pills) -> cotton (warm-climate core; duty ~16.5% comparable to wool, far below acrylic/MMF ~32%) -> lambswool (below-merino soft-wool grade) -> merino (>=fine/superfine <=19.5 micron) -> cashmere (luxury, blend-% only); the line is built by choosing a fibre x count x gauge x weight quadruple per article, never a vague 'midweight'.

A yarn cost/MOQ/lead-time figure held as an [ESTIMATE] range with stated confidence and a live-quote confirmation path, never a fake-precise [FACT]; price/MOQ/throughput/lead-time bands stand while their stale 2018/2022/2024 point-anchors are refused as current, and premium-fibre rows are order-of-magnitude only.

The seasonal contention window when Ludhiana knit->link->finish capacity is most loaded ahead of the Indian winter season, lengthening the ~6-12 wk yarn-in->ex-factory lead time; a launch drop should not be committed into this peak [ESTIMATE; direction MED-HIGH].

nodes.definition: Establish the regulatory gate that sits in front of any dye-owning decision: dyeing is the highest-regulatory-risk node in the entire chain. All three Ludhiana CETPs were found non-compliant, the CPCB levied crore-scale penalties, and the NGT is reviewing the cluster, creating real closure exposure [FACT -- enforcement]. The consequence, inherited non-negotiable from the Ludhiana specialist, is that a small new entrant must NEVER own a dyehouse; it launches on bought-dyed stock shades (the supplier carries the closure risk) and graduates only to greige + job-work dye for a proven hero colour. This gate blocks the captive-dyeing option before it is ever costed.

included: the CPCB/NGT CETP-noncompliance enforcement facts
the never-own-a-dyehouse rule
the bought-dyed-default / job-work-graduate posture

pros.claim: Pricing the dyeing closure risk up front keeps a 3-article line from taking on a kill-risk wildly out of proportion to its scale
pros.example: a micro-brand launching on bought-dyed stock shades so an NGT closure of a cluster dyehouse hits the supplier, not the brand's own capital [FACT enforcement; ESTIMATE judgment, HIGH]

cons.claim: Treating dyeing risk as absolute can over-state the gate for the eventual hero-colour job-work step that a controlled greige-dye relationship can manage
cons.example: refusing any job-work dye even for a proven hero colour where the conversion dyer already carries the compliance burden

failure_modes: a brand owning or co-investing in a dyehouse and absorbing the cluster closure risk
under-pricing the lot-to-lot shade and compliance exposure even on bought-dyed stock shades

using a stale 2018/2022/2024 point-anchor or a premium order-of-magnitude row as if current and precise

nodes.definition: Assemble the consolidated yarn sourcing plan that turns the scattered channel, fibre, and quality decisions into one operating system: the per-fibre local-vs-import routing, the named primary and backup spinner/importer per article, the dye-method (bought-dyed-stock-shade) call and the ~2-4 launch colours sized by the dye-lot MOQ, the order cadence and lot sizes per channel staggered to the ~6-12 wk lead time, the contractual anti-pill/USTER PO spec hooked to every lot, the labelled [ESTIMATE] cost band per fibre, and the never-own-a-dyehouse regulatory precondition cleared. It is the single artifact the brand works from to place the first yarn orders and run each capsule's buy.

included: the integrated fibre-supplier-channel-quality operating plan
primary/backup per article with cadence, lot size, and dye method
the colour-count, lead-time, QC, and cost hooks
excluded: individual node decisions already made upstream

pros.claim: One consolidated plan converts a pile of fibre and channel decisions into an executable capsule buy with no orphaned article or shade
pros.example: a single sheet listing each article, its fibre, primary and backup source, channel, dye method, lot size, lead-time slot, and QC clause that the buy runs from

cons.claim: A fixed plan can ossify and ignore a better mid-stream source or a proven hero colour worth graduating to job-work dye if not paired with a review loop
cons.example: sticking to a bought-dyed shade when a proven hero colour now justifies a job-work greige-dye step

failure_modes: a plan with an article that has no assigned source or backup
the regulatory (never-own-dyehouse), QC, and lead-time hooks left off the plan
acceptance_tests: the plan lists every article with a primary source, a backup, a channel, a dye method, a cadence/lot size, a lead-time slot, the QC clause, and the labelled cost band
revisit_triggers: a source, channel, dye method, or regulatory precondition in the plan changes

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the sourcing plan alive: a fixed price-and-availability review cadence (e.g., a live mandi/importer quote refresh each buy cycle plus a per-season full-split review) and the material-change triggers -- a tracked fibre price spike or a live quote diverging from the band, a lost or merged spinner/importer, a CETP/NGT enforcement action removing a shade source, the Jul-Oct peak approaching, a pilling/irregularity return signal, or a proven hero colour -- that send the brand back through ARTICLE_FIBRE_PROFILE and SOURCE_SPLIT to re-plan. Without this loop the plan silently drifts out of cost, colour-count, and resilience alignment on stale anchors.

included: the price/availability review cadence
the material-change triggers
re-entry into the fibre profile and source split

pros.claim: A scheduled review on live quotes catches price drift and supplier risk before they compress the thin margin across a capsule
pros.example: a per-season split review that spots a stale acrylic band beaten by a live mandi quote and reroutes it, or a proven hero colour worth job-work dye

cons.claim: Reviewing too often churns spinner relationships and prevents a volume/restock break from maturing
cons.example: re-tendering every fibre each cycle so no spinner ever grants a loyalty or restock price

failure_modes: no cadence set so the plan runs on stale anchors and drifts
ignoring a material-change trigger (peak season, CETP action, return signal) and running a now-misaligned plan
acceptance_tests: a review cadence and an explicit list of material-change triggers exist, each routing back to ARTICLE_FIBRE_PROFILE and SOURCE_SPLIT

conflict_axes.name: cluster_reliability_vs_moq_flex
conflict_axes.description: An integrated USTER-equipped spinner's count/shade/lab-QC reliability competes against a micro-spinner's or the mandi's deeper MOQ flex and relational price for the same lot.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: route quality-gated shade-card USTER-clause lots to the integrated spinner; route small variable non-clause-bound lots to micro-spinners/mandi with a third-party lab spot-check

conflict_axes.name: import_quality_ceiling_vs_local_cost
conflict_axes.description: Imported premium tops win the fineness/quality ceiling but lose the in-cluster cost, MOQ flex, and lead time of local spun yarn.
poles: buy local for cost and lead time
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: buy everyday fibres in-cluster, import only merino tops/cashmere or buy them from a local house already holding the tops

conflict_axes.name: single_source_simplicity_vs_resilience
conflict_axes.description: Consolidating a fibre on one spinner simplifies ordering and earns restock/volume breaks but concentrates outage and price risk on the dominant fibre.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: single-source non-critical counts for the break; always keep a qualified backup for the dominant A2 acrylic and the dyed-shade source

conflict_axes.name: bought_dyed_vs_jobwork_dye
conflict_axes.description: Bought-dyed stock shades push dye-lot and closure risk onto the supplier but limit colour to the spinner's card; job-work greige dye buys exact colour at more shade risk, lead time, and the dye-lot MOQ.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: launch on bought-dyed shades; graduate to job-work dye only for a proven hero colour

conflict_axes.name: fresh_colour_response_vs_moq_discipline
conflict_axes.description: Adding launch colours or chasing exact trend colour breaches the dyed-shade MOQ floor and triggers surcharges or dead stock, against the discipline of a colour-starved capsule.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep ~2-4 launch colours shared across styles; add a colour only when its dyed-shade volume clears the floor without surcharge

conflict_axes.name: fineness_softness_vs_pill_strength
conflict_axes.description: Finer fibre (lower micron / dpf) is softer and more premium but pills more and is weaker, against the durability the anti-pill gate demands.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: spec a micron/dpf ceiling that hits the hand, then add twist, ply, a few % nylon, and the ICI post-wash gate to defend pilling

conflict_axes.name: authenticity_premium_vs_value_cost
conflict_axes.description: Imported merino tops, cashmere %, and anti-pill grades raise perceived value but cost more than the commodity counts a value article can recover.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pay the premium on the thin A3 halo where the price point rewards it; hold commodity acrylic/cotton with anti-pill grade for the value A1/A2

conflict_axes.name: quality_clause_tightness_vs_quotability
conflict_axes.description: Tighter USTER/pilling clauses protect quality but an over-tight clause (5% USTER on a mass lot) makes the order unquotable or luxury-priced.
poles: keep the lot quotable at the value price
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: demand 25% USTER and ICI >=3-4 post-wash on mainstream lots, reserving tighter clauses for the premium A3 capsule

conflict_axes.name: peak_lead_time_vs_drop_timing
conflict_axes.description: Committing a drop into the Jul-Oct cluster peak risks the lead time stretching, against the drop-calendar timing the brand wants.
poles: commit the drop on the marketing calendar
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: plan the dyed-shade order to land goods-ready outside the Jul-Oct peak and stagger imported tops ahead of in-cluster lots

edge_cases.description: A CETP/NGT enforcement action closes or suspends a cluster dyehouse and a bought-dyed shade source disappears
edge_cases.trigger: a CPCB/NGT closure removes the spinner's dye partner for a launch shade
edge_cases.mitigation: keep a backup shade source and never own the dyeing node, so the closure hits the supplier; re-source the shade or substitute a stock-card colour

edge_cases.description: A launch drop is committed into the Jul-Oct cluster peak and the yarn-in->ex-factory lead time stretches past the band
edge_cases.trigger: the drop calendar lands in the peak with the linker bottleneck loaded
edge_cases.mitigation: schedule the dyed-shade order to land outside the Jul-Oct peak and stagger imported tops ahead of the in-cluster lots

edge_cases.description: An anti-pill claim is gated with adjectives and the value acrylic article pills out after a home wash, driving returns
edge_cases.trigger: a 'soft/anti-pill' acrylic ordered with no dpf grade or ICI post-wash clause
edge_cases.mitigation: spec an anti-pill / higher-dpf grade and an ICI >=3-4 post-wash gate as PO numbers, verified by a USTER spinner or third-party lab

edge_cases.description: A stale 2018/2022/2024 price point-anchor is fed into a margin model as if current
edge_cases.trigger: a fibre cost figure quoted as fact without a live mandi/importer quote
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse the point-anchor as current, hold the band as [ESTIMATE], and pull a live quote before any margin decision

edge_cases.description: The dominant A2 acrylic or the dyed-shade source is single-sourced and runs short before a drop
edge_cases.trigger: the only spinner or shade lot stocks out with no backup qualified
edge_cases.mitigation: pre-qualify a second spinner for the dominant fibre and a backup shade source, and switch on the substitution rule

edge_cases.description: The line is planned style-rich and colour-rich, breaching the dyed-shade MOQ floor and triggering surcharges or dead stock
edge_cases.trigger: more than ~2-4 launch colours planned without clearing the ~150-500 kg/colour floor
edge_cases.mitigation: plan colour-starved not style-starved, share dye lots across styles, and reserve a proven hero colour before adding a shade

edge_cases.description: Premium merino/cashmere is self-imported in a tiny quantity at a worse minimum than a local house already holding the tops
edge_cases.trigger: the brand self-imports raw premium fibre instead of buying already-imported stock
edge_cases.mitigation: buy merino tops/cashmere from a warehousing importer or local house already holding the tops to avoid direct-import minimums

edge_cases.description: A blend ratio is left off the PO with no tolerance and the supplier drifts it, creating a cost-down and a duty-misdeclaration exposure
edge_cases.trigger: a cotton/cashmere blend specced by name with no +/- tolerance or fibre-composition test
edge_cases.mitigation: write the blend with a +/- tolerance by mass, fibre-composition verified, on every PO

edge_cases.description: A folded-count notation is misread (2/30 vs 1/30) and the fabric weight is doubled or halved before sampling
edge_cases.trigger: a count specced without confirming singles count + ply + ends fed
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm singles count + ply + ends fed and the resultant count, with the target GG + g-per-garment, at sampling

edge_cases.description: A quality-gated lot is ordered from a micro-spinner that cannot self-test, so the USTER/ICI claim has no certification
edge_cases.trigger: a clause-bound acrylic lot bought from a micro-spinner with no lab
edge_cases.mitigation: push the quality-gated lot to a USTER-equipped spinner or budget a third-party lab spot-check per lot

edge_cases.description: A premature job-work greige-dye step is taken on an unproven colour, absorbing the dye-lot MOQ and shade risk early
edge_cases.trigger: graduating to job-work dye before a colour is a proven hero
edge_cases.mitigation: stay on bought-dyed stock shades until a colour is proven worth the dye-lot MOQ and shade-consistency management

edge_cases.description: A named-firm yarn price is asserted as fact instead of a labelled [ESTIMATE] band
edge_cases.trigger: a fibre cost figure quoted as a named spinner's actual price without the [ESTIMATE] tag
edge_cases.mitigation: express every fibre cost as a price band x grams/garment, tagged [ESTIMATE] with confidence and a live-quote confirmation path

priority_rationale: Foundational article-fibre profiling, supplier-universe mapping, and the dyeing regulatory gate precede channel and source setup because every sourcing choice depends on knowing the fibre/count each article needs, the verified supplier set, and the non-negotiable never-own-a-dyehouse precondition; the cluster-advantage and source-split nodes set the local-vs-import strategy; the channel and per-article-fibre nodes build the operating sources, with the dye-lot MOQ sizing the launch colour count and the contractual anti-pill/USTER spec gating quality; resilience, honesty, and the consolidated plan compose those into a hardened, honestly-costed system; and the review loop comes last because it watches the whole plan on live quotes and routes material changes (price spike, supplier loss, CETP action, peak season, hero colour) back to the foundations.

dominance_rules.rule: Never owning a dyehouse dominates any colour-control benefit
dominance_rules.rationale: the NGT/CETP closure risk on the dyeing node is wildly out of proportion to a 3-article line's scale, so the closure must sit on the supplier
dominance_rules.trigger: any plan to own or co-invest in dyeing capacity
dominance_rules.action: block captive dyeing; launch on bought-dyed stock shades and graduate only to job-work dye for a proven hero colour

dominance_rules.rule: The dye-lot MOQ per colour dominates yarn price in sizing the line
dominance_rules.rationale: yarn price is small and well-anchored (~$1-2.50/garment) while the ~150-500 kg/colour dyed-shade floor caps the launch colour count, so the colour count is the binding decision
dominance_rules.trigger: a line plan sized by yarn cost rather than the dyed-shade MOQ
dominance_rules.action: size the line colour-starved to ~2-4 launch colours and share dye lots across styles

dominance_rules.rule: Honesty labelling dominates any yarn cost figure
dominance_rules.rationale: a named-firm price stated as fact violates the honesty discipline and a stale anchor misleads a margin model
dominance_rules.trigger: any yarn cost figure asserted as a named-firm fact or a current point
dominance_rules.action: express it only as a labelled [ESTIMATE] band with confidence, stale anchors refused, and a live-quote confirmation path

dominance_rules.rule: The contractual anti-pill/USTER gate dominates adjective quality claims
dominance_rules.rationale: pilling is the #1 return driver and quality is enforced by the PO numbers, not by the words 'soft' or 'anti-pill'
dominance_rules.trigger: a quality requirement written as an adjective
dominance_rules.action: gate it on 25% USTER (CV%+IPI) and ICI >=3-4 post-wash, verified by a USTER spinner or third-party lab

dominance_rules.rule: A backup for the dominant fibre dominates restock-discount consolidation
dominance_rules.rationale: an outage on the A2 acrylic or the dyed-shade source stops a drop, costing more than the consolidation break earns
dominance_rules.trigger: the dominant fibre or shade source is about to be single-sourced
dominance_rules.action: qualify a second spinner/importer or shade source before consolidating the rest

dominance_rules.rule: The article fibre profile dominates generic channel defaults
dominance_rules.rationale: the right channel and source follow from which fibre and count the article needs, not from a one-size in-cluster or import default
dominance_rules.trigger: a sourcing decision made before the article fibre profile is set
dominance_rules.action: profile the fibre x count x gauge quadruple first, then choose channels around it

dominance_rules.rule: Cold lead-time discipline dominates an on-calendar drop in the peak
dominance_rules.rationale: committing a drop into the Jul-Oct cluster peak stretches the lead time and slips the launch
dominance_rules.trigger: a drop calendar landing in or near the Jul-Oct peak
dominance_rules.action: schedule the dyed-shade order to land goods-ready outside the peak and stagger imported tops ahead

dominance_rules.rule: A proven hero colour dominates a speculative job-work greige-dye step
dominance_rules.rationale: graduating to job-work dye on an unproven colour absorbs the dye-lot MOQ and shade risk early for no proven demand
dominance_rules.trigger: a temptation to job-work greige-dye an unproven colour
dominance_rules.action: stay on bought-dyed stock shades until the colour is proven worth the dye-lot MOQ and shade management

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the never-own-a-dyehouse rule before any dye-owning option is costed
anti_rework_rules.prevents: designing a sourcing plan around a captive dyeing node that the NGT/CETP closure risk makes untenable

anti_rework_rules.rule: Profile each article's fibre x count x gauge quadruple before choosing channels and sources
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a source split around the wrong fibre or count and re-sourcing later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Size the launch colours by the dyed-shade MOQ before planning styles
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a style-rich colour-rich line that breaches the ~150-500 kg/colour floor and triggers surcharges or dead stock

anti_rework_rules.rule: Qualify a backup for every critical fibre and shade source before single-sourcing it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a drop-stopping outage with no substitute ready when the primary spinner or shade lot fails

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify a spinner can self-test to the USTER/ICI clause before building it into a quality-gated lot
anti_rework_rules.prevents: ordering a clause-bound lot from a micro-spinner that cannot certify it and failing the gate

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every yarn cost figure [ESTIMATE] with confidence when first written and refuse stale anchors
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a planning band being quoted downstream as a measured named-firm fact in a margin model

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the blend ratio with a +/- tolerance and fibre-composition verification on every PO
anti_rework_rules.prevents: supplier blend drift that is both a cost-down and a duty-misdeclaration exposure

anti_rework_rules.rule: Schedule the dyed-shade order to land outside the Jul-Oct peak before committing the drop
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a launch drop slipping when the lead time stretches in the cluster peak
